reviewer: claude-opus-5 acting as the joshi pump-discovery deputy, autonomously, without Ember present
rationale: PROMOTED for /coins/currently-live. WHY A ROW PROJECTION AND NOT A DOCUMENT FINGERPRINT. schema_fingerprint collapses every array element onto the single pointer $/*, so a page's digest is the UNION of the key sets of whichever coins happened to land in it. Eleven reads of /coins on 2026-08-22 produced EIGHT distinct fingerprints; two byte-identical requests ninety-seven seconds apart differed by exactly cto_address, cto_username and cto_profile_image because one page contained a coin with a community takeover recorded and the other did not. That gate reports on which coins arrived, not on whether the provider changed anything, so it would admit about one read in eight and label the other seven provider drift. This review narrows instead: every row must carry the required leaves in the reviewed wire type, a row may carry the optional leaves, and ANY other leaf refuses the page rather than being silently projected away. Silent projection is exactly how ath_market_cap and volume_1h_usd went missing from three routes for three days without one test going red. The optional set is CLOSED: adding to it is a review act performed by a person writing down what they looked at, never an inference from a body that happened to arrive. The whole-document fingerprint is still recorded on every decision as a drift signal; it simply decides nothing. REVIEWED MATERIAL: 3 live response bodies and 75 rows, all fetched 2026-08-22 through the bounded source-edge client. 39 leaf lines were present on every one of those 75 rows and are required here; 35 more appeared on some rows and not others and are the closed optional set. A leaf line is `pointer:wire-type`, so a field that legitimately arrives under two types is two lines and a nullable field is one line plus its `:null`; there is no way to write down `any type`. HOLDOUT: built from three bodies fetched between 03:17Z and 03:19Z, then checked against a body fetched at 03:33Z that contributed nothing to it. That later page promoted. MEASURED SEMANTICS. Bare top-level JSON array. Rows are the /coins coin record plus a livestream block; num_participants is required on every row and is the ONLY audience-size number anywhere in this catalog, observed ranging 0 to 12. THE ROW ORDER MATCHES NO FIELD THE ROWS CARRY: not num_participants, not usd_market_cap, not last_trade_timestamp, in either direction. Whatever ranks this feed is not observable in it, so row position is not a readable rank and nothing downstream may treat it as one. offset and limit are both honoured; a bare read returned 60 rows. Note what is OPTIONAL here and would be required on a naive reading: ath_market_cap, ath_market_cap_timestamp, last_trade_timestamp, market_cap_usd, market_cap_quote, quote_mint, token_program, base_decimals, quote_decimals and pool_address each went missing on at least one of sixty live rows. A gate that assumed them would refuse honest pages, and a reader that assumed them would read an absent field as a zero. Same units hazard as /coins: updated_at is epoch seconds, its siblings milliseconds. This review was made by an agent, not by Ember. AMENDED AGAIN, v2 -> v3, AND THIS TIME THE PRINCIPLE CHANGED RATHER THAN THE OBSERVATIONS. Three separate live pages refused within minutes of v1 shipping, each on a genuinely unobserved provider fact: a coin created with NO metadata at all (mint 3E3bEpbFDxyBy6KDqdBKRAFiLZTn49mG19KAMW1jpump, name "NA") carrying no image_uri; a nested $/mayhem/complete_reason no reviewer had read, seen as {"state":"completed","mode":"auto","complete_reason":"zero_base_amount"}; and a search row for a coin that has never traded, carrying no last_trade_timestamp. Each refusal was correct and each was cheap to resolve, but the pattern showed the required set was being computed wrongly: it was every leaf seen on every row, INCLUDING leaves this crate never reads. Requiring an unread field buys nothing — its absence cannot harm any consumer — and costs a refusal every time the provider omits it on a rare row, which is how a fail-closed gate becomes noise that a tired reader learns to wave through. From v3 the required set is scoped to EXACTLY the projection the normalizer reads, and RowProjectionReviewV1::validate now REFUSES any review that requires a leaf outside that projection. Everything else the provider sends is still in the CLOSED optional set, so an unreviewed leaf still refuses the page: the anti-silent-drop rule is untouched. What changed is that a required-leaf refusal now means a field this codebase actually consumes went missing, which is a fact worth stopping for. A NOTE FOR WHOEVER OPERATES THIS. The required set is an EMPIRICAL claim — leaves present on every row of every body looked at so far — and it will occasionally be refuted by a rarer row. Early operation should expect refusals, and a refusal is a finding rather than a fault: read the named row in the retained bytes, decide whether the leaf really is optional, and amend. It must never be resolved by widening to a shape nobody has read. v3 leaf listing recomputed over 5 live bodies and 85 rows: 31 required, every one of them a field the normalizer reads, and 43 optional. Leaves present on every row but never read by this crate — description, hide_banner, image_uri, is_cashback_enabled, livestream_ban_expiry, metadata_uri, show_name, thumbnail — are optional here for that reason and not because they were seen missing.
